categories.means: Cannot sign in, OTP or SMS code not arriving, biometric or face check failing, locked out, device change or re-registration trouble
A transfer, bill payment, airtime or card payment fails, hangs on processing, or is slow
Money missing or debited without value, reversals not received, wrong or hidden balance, transaction history missing or wrong
Crashes, freezes, slow to open or load, network error messages, downtime, app not working at all (without a clearer cause above)
Complaints about fees, stamp duty, SMS charges, deductions the reviewer thinks are wrong or too high
Design, layout, navigation, an update that changed things, hard to find a feature, confusing screens
Asks for something the app does not have or should add
Customer service, complaints not resolved, no reply, branch or call centre experience, disputes
Worry or report of fraud, unauthorised access, account compromised, scam
Gibberish, empty praise or complaint with no content, off-topic, not about the app or the service

tie_breaks: If a review names a concrete failure, use that failure's category, not app_stability. 'Can't transfer, app is slow' is transfers_payments first, app_stability second.
money_balance beats transfers_payments when money has actually left the account or vanished. A failed transfer with no money taken is transfers_payments.
login_access beats app_stability when the only thing the reviewer cannot do is sign in.
Mixed praise and complaint: the complaint is the category. Add praise as a second category only if it is a real part of the review.
Use the second category only when the review clearly raises a second, separate issue.
Unreadable, gibberish or decorative text: other, severity 1.
Ignore the star rating or any rating mentioned outside the text. Label what the reviewer wrote.

severity.1: Annoyance. Unhappy but could still do what they came to do. Includes praise and other.
severity.2: Blocked a task. Could not complete something (log in, transfer, see history), with no sign of money lost or being stuck for days.
severity.3: Money lost, stuck or locked out. Money debited or missing, unable to use the account or app for days or more, or an urgent need failed.

severity_rule: When torn between two levels, choose the lower one.
